request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Patient Name: Not Specified
Medical Record Number: Not Specified
Date of Admission: Not Specified
Date of Discharge: Not Specified

INTRODUCTION:
The patient is an 81-year-old woman who visited the department of internal medicine in our hospital with complaints of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, and an upper abdominal mass. She had a history of left breast cancer 11 years ago. The patient was diagnosed with peritoneal metastasis of recurrent breast cancer and was put on endocrine therapy using letrozole.

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient's symptoms improved with endocrine therapy, and she showed recovery from pleural metastasis and pleural effusion. Tumor marker values fluctuated during the course of treatment, with no abnormal CEA values obtained, and CA15-3 and BCA225 values gradually declining from the time of recurrence and returning to normal levels 2 years later. NCC-ST-439 value gradually increased up to 49 U/ml 6 months later, with a gradual decline thereafter along with the other tumor markers. The patient was currently receiving treatment in the outpatient department and is still alive on the same medication.

DISCHARGE OUTCOME:
The patient is being discharged in stable condition with continued endocrine therapy.

FOLLOW-UP:
No relapse of malignancy has been detected after a period of 6 years.

ATTENDING PHYSICIAN:
Not Specified
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Letrozole.

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Continue endocrine therapy as prescribed. Follow up with your healthcare provider as recommended.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode concerns recurrent breast cancer with peritoneal metastasis, treated with endocrine therapy (letrozole).

Coding options:
- C50 is the primary breast malignancy. The breast cancer was 11 years ago, and the patient is not documented as having active primary disease in the breast.
- C78.6 is secondary malignant neoplasm of the retroperitoneum and peritoneum. The condition treated is the peritoneal metastasis, so this is the best fit for the principal diagnosis.
- Z85.3 is personal history of breast cancer. It would apply only if no active disease were present, which is not the case here.

Under ICD-10-AM coding rules, when a secondary site is the focus of treatment and the primary has been previously excised or eradicated with no current evidence of it, the secondary site is coded as principal. Here the treatment is directed at the peritoneal metastasis, so C78 is the category.

CODE: C78
